answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pooling the stake of identities that share the same resources and slashing the whole pool when one misbehaves. Like water seeping through karst, hidden links between accounts surface over time as they draw from the same nectar of shared rewards, reuse the same tools, and repeat the same patterns. A lone honest identity risks little, but each extra fake identity enlarges the shared pool, so a single detected fraud whispers through the whole cluster and wipes out everything the attacker built, making the marginal fake more expensive than the last.
